Case: Erin is a 38-year-old who presents with 6 months of shoulder pain and progressive hand weakness. Erin reports that her pain started after a car accident, and has not improved despite trying ibuprofen, acetaminophen and physical therapy. A steroid injection did relieve some of the pain, but she says this was short-lived and she feels that she is reaching a breaking point with the pain. During your physical exam, you note that she has some weakness on shoulder abduction and bilateral Hoffman's signs. The neurosurgeon advised that Erin would need an anterior spine surgery, but Erin declined at that time. Repeat CT and MRi of the cervical spine confirm a disc herniation at C4-5 with slight progression in the canal stenosis.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Erin? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
